newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Kenda, U.S. Cooper in China tyre venture.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Kenda, U.S. Cooper in China tyre venture.

text.p: Taiwan's Kenda Rubber Industrial Co Ltd and U.S. maker Cooper Tire & Rubber Co are forming a US$50 million venture to make radial tyres in China's Jiangsu province, Kenda said on Wednesday.
"Kenda is now negotiating with Cooper about the venture, hoping to use Cooper's technology to jointly make radial tyres for passenger cars in Jiangsu," a Kenda spokesman told Reuters.
"The deal has yet to be finalised," he said.
Kenda would hold 70 percent of the venture, with the remainder taken by Cooper, he said.
Kenda would start construction by the end of 1996, with completion seen in 1998, he said.

The proposal for a radial tyre factory, which must win Chinese government approval, is a modification of an already approved Kenda investment in a US$30 million plant to make bias tyres for bicycles and motorcycles, he said.
Kenda already has a tyre factory in Shenzhen, adjacent to Hong Kong, which started producing tyres for bicycles and motrocycles in 1993.
The US$30 million Shenzhen plant should generate 1996 pretax profit of T$200 million on sales of T$2 billion, he said.
